(2) notes/notes_stratonovich_ham_second_moment.tex replaces the smoothing and truncation sentence of L:damped-homogeneous-norms by the multiplier comparison E:damped-multiplier-comparison (statement 826-847, display 836-841, proof 894-917). ## OccupationCeilingFinite (whole result)

Wave L8, item c2, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/OccupationCeilingFinite.lean`.
It proves the boundedness claim of `P:variational-positive-scores`
(`VariationalRate.S1Bdd`, `notes/integrated_unmasked_variational.tex` lines
272-274 at `a284420`) deterministically, and the occupation ceiling of
`T:intrinsic-occupation-ceiling` (`notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex`
lines 205-220, proof 222-250) with the constant `K_0 R_sp` in place of
`C_occ`, both over one named input `SpaceTimeCS alpha0 Gamma` (step (c) of
the route; proved under `H:homog` by `SpaceTimePositivity.spaceTimeCS_holds`
and discharged in `L8Completed` (`spaceTimeCS_completed`), so after integration nothing is supplied). Standing assumptions (occupation file lines 4-21,
unmasked file line 4): a nonzero covariance satisfying `H:homog`
(`HomogCovariance d alpha alpha0 Gamma mu`, `Gamma != 0`) and `a = alpha0`
(written by using `alpha0` for `a`). `I_Psi = int_0^1 lambda_(Psi,s) ds`
with `lambda` the square root of the supremum of the real Rayleigh quotient
(`VariationalDilation.integratedRate`, `rate`), and `v_Psi` is the
integral-form cost `VariationalDilation.rawCost`. `K0 a = 2^a/(1-a)` and
`ceilingValue alpha c C` (`U_c` with a real `C`) have the same bodies as
`SpatialBracket.K0` and `SpatialBracket.ceilingValue`, and the conclusion of
`occupation_ceiling_K0_paper` is literally
`SpatialBracket.OccupationCeilingK0 alpha alpha0 Gamma`. Proof route (Le's
decision 3 of wave L8; the TeX proves the boundedness stochastically, lines
309-325 via `T:full-upper`, and the ceiling through the countable measurable
selection `L:occupation-rayleigh-selection`, lines 149-193, the map `Q` and
`rho_g` of `L:occupation-raw-square`, and the class `O`): (a)
`exists_unitTest_gt`, near-optimal real unit test functions for the Rayleigh
supremum of the bounded potential `h_(Psi,s)`; (b) `exists_near_field`, a
finite partition of unity `chi_i` in time and the field
`G(s,x) = sum_i chi_i(s) f_i(x)^2` (`fieldG`), with
`int_0^1 lambda_s^2 - eps <= int_0^1 int h_s G_s - T(G)`,
`T(G) = int_0^1 sum_i chi_i b(f_i)` (`fieldT`), from Lipschitz bounds in `s`;
(c) the named input: Cauchy-Schwarz for the space-time form `stForm`,
`stForm(Psi,Psi) = v_Psi` and `int int h_s Phi_s = stForm(Psi,Phi)`, for
`Psi` in `C_pos` and nonnegative continuous compactly supported `Phi`; (d)
`field_energy_le`, `F(G,G) <= K_0 R_0 T(G)^(alpha/2)` from the square bound
for unit tests (`pair_unit_le`), the sharp Schur row `K_0`
(`row_le`, `schur_sharp`; intrinsic file lines 42-49) and discrete and
integral Jensen; (e) `integratedRate_sq_le` and `score_le_ceiling`, by the
two weighted AM-GM bounds `young_quarter`, `young_q` and the power algebra
`ceilingValue_eq`. `R_0` (`SpatialSmoothRatio.R0`) and `R_sp`
(`SpatialFourLinear.Rsp`) are equal under the standing assumptions
(`SpatialOccupationL7Completed.spatial_ratio_H1_paper_completed`); the
internal theorems use `R_0`, the `_paper` ceilings `R_sp`. `stForm` here is the
iterated Bochner integral; it is bounded from above only for nonnegative
integrands through lower integrals (`integral_le_toReal_lintegral`), and its
other values come from the named input, so no junk value enters an upper
bound. `S_c^pos` (`sSup`) is used only with nonemptiness and boundedness
proved. Re-issued without `S1Bdd` (over `SpaceTimeCS`; sources unchanged):
`variational_positive_scores_sSup_st_paper`,
`spatial_static_score_sSup_st_paper`, `spatial_smooth_score_sSup_st_paper`,
`R0_le_of_st_paper`, `spatial_static_energy_score_sSup_st_paper`. Narrower
than the TeX: the ceiling constant is `K_0 R_sp`, an upper bound of `C_occ`
(`P:raw-occupation-energy`, line 96), so the Lean ceiling is the larger
number; the class `O`, `A(g)`, `C_occ`, `E_zeta^O`, `L:occupation-raw-square`
(see `SpaceTimePositivity`), `P:raw-occupation-energy` and the selection lemma
are not formalized; the second form `c^m (2 zeta)^(alpha/(2k)) F_0(E_zeta^O)`
of `E:occupation-score-ceiling`, the moment statement `C_2 <= U_2` (which
needs `T:intrinsic-second-moment`) and the zero-covariance paragraph (lines
302-308) are not formalized; `Q_2 >= S_2^pos` remains unformalized. Every
hypothesis of each wrapper is used (`Gamma != 0` through `R0_bound`).

## SpaceTimePositivity (whole result)

Wave L8, item c1, in `StratonovichHAMSecondMoment/SpaceTimePositivity.lean`.
It proves, with nothing supplied, the space-time facts that the deterministic
proof of the boundedness claim of `P:variational-positive-scores` needs, and
states narrower forms of two lemmas. TeX at `a284420`:
`notes/integrated_occupation_ceiling.tex` (standing assumptions lines 4-21,
`E:raw-occupation-definitions` lines 10-18, `L:occupation-raw-square`
statement lines 23-42 with `E:occupation-raw-identities` lines 33-37 and the
bound of line 40, proof lines 44-90) and
`notes/integrated_intrinsic_constant.tex` (`L:positive-raw-embedding`
statement lines 22-39 with `E:positive-bochner-inclusion` lines 26-30 and
`E:positive-raw-mean` lines 33-36; `E:positive-local-spatial-bound` lines
70-73). The cost `v_Psi`, the mean `h_(Psi,s)` and the class `C_pos` are
reused from `VariationalDilation` (`rawCost`, `mean`, `CPos`: integral forms of
`E:compact-raw-cost` and `E:compact-raw-mean`). The physical pairing
`B_Gamma(F,G) = int (int F(x) G(x-y) dx) Gamma(dy)` is
`SpatialFourierBound.spatialPair`. New objects: `stPair` (the pairing of the
time slices `Phi1(s,.)`, `Phi2(t,.)`) and the space-time form
`stForm a Gamma Phi1 Phi2 = int_(0,1)^2 |s-t|^(-a) B_Gamma(Phi1(s,.), Phi2(t,.))`,
a Bochner integral for the product Lebesgue measure on `(0,1)^2`. It is the
integral of `E:positive-bochner-inclusion` with `G = H_sp` written through
the physical pairing, and `A(g)` of `E:raw-occupation-definitions` at
`Phi1 = Phi2 = g^2`. `stFormIter` is the same form as an iterated integral,
verbatim `OccupationCeilingFinite.stForm`, and `stFormIter_eq` identifies the
two for continuous compactly supported fields. Every field in the statements
is a continuous compactly supported real function on `R x R^d`; the TeX's
fields live in `L^2(I; H_sp)`. Implicit hypotheses made explicit: `a < 1` for
integrability, `0 < a` for positivity (the mixture representation of the
kernel needs it), local finiteness of `Gamma` in place of the physical
covariance bound `E:positive-local-spatial-bound`, evenness of `Gamma` for
symmetry. Integrability of every integrand is a conclusion
(`stIntegrand_integrable` and the first two conjuncts of the mean
identities), so no statement holds through Lean's value `0` of a
non-integrable Bochner integral. Proof route (the TeX works in the completed
Hilbert spaces `H_sp` and `H_t (x) H_sp`): spatial positivity
`B_Gamma(Q,Q) >= 0` for continuous compactly supported `Q` by uniform
approximation with mollified test functions; positivity of `stForm` by writing
`|s-t|^(-a)` as a positive mixture of rank-one kernels
(`TimeCompletion.kern_eq_mixture`) and Fubini (`weighted_stPair`);
Cauchy-Schwarz by the discriminant; the identities by Fubini
(`spatialPair_eq_conv`, `integral_mean_mul_eq_stForm_swap`). Wrappers:
`space_time_positivity_homog` (all facts under `H:homog` with `a = alpha0`,
`Gamma != 0` not assumed); `spaceTimeCS_holds` (the proposition `SpaceTimeCS
alpha0 Gamma`, whose fields are definitionally those of
`OccupationCeilingFinite.SpaceTimeCS`; its nonnegativity hypothesis on the
field is not needed); `occupation_raw_square_cc_paper` and
`positive_raw_variance_form_paper` with the sections' standing assumptions
(`H:homog`, `a = alpha0`, `Gamma != 0`; `Gamma != 0` is carried and not used,
the parameter is named `_hΓ`). Narrower conclusions: for
`L:occupation-raw-square`, the profile class is continuous compactly
supported fields `g` in place of the class `O` (no unit-norm condition is
needed), and only the integral forms are proved (`A(g) >= 0` as a genuine
integral, the pairing `int_I int h_(Psi,t) g_t^2 = F(Psi, g^2)`, and the bound
by `sqrt(v_Psi A(g))`); for `L:positive-raw-embedding`, only the variance
identity `F(Psi,Psi) = v_Psi` with integrability and `v_Psi >= 0`. Not
formalized: `H_sp`, the map `Q`, `rho_g` in `H_I` and
`||rho_g||^2 = A(g)`; `H_t`, `H_I`, `J_G` and its bound by `K_0` (the scalar
Schur bound is `OccupationCeilingFinite.schur_sharp`); the mean identity
`T_R Psi(s) = B_E(m_R h_(Psi,s))` and the canonical versions of
`L:positive-raw-embedding`. Supplied inputs: none.

   124	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: if `F` vanishes for `|x| > R` and `G` vanishes for
   125	`|x| > R`, then the inner integral `y ↦ ∫ F(x) G(x-y) dx` of `B_Γ(F,G)` vanishes for
   126	`|y| > 2R`. -/
   127	theorem cross_eq_zero {F G : Rd d → ℝ} {R : ℝ} (hFR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → F x = 0)
   128	    (hGR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → G x = 0) {y : Rd d} (hy : 2 * R < ‖y‖) :
   129	    ∫ x, F x * G (x - y) = 0 := by
   130	  have h : ∀ x, F x * G (x - y) = 0 := by
   131	    intro x
   132	    by_cases hx : R < ‖x‖
   133	    · rw [hFR x hx, zero_mul]
   134	    · have h1 : ‖y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + ‖x - y‖ := by
   135	        have := norm_sub_le x (x - y)
   136	        simpa using this
   137	      rw [hGR (x - y) (by linarith), mul_zero]
   138	  simp [h]

   140	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route: the inner integral is bounded,
   141	`|∫ F(x) G(x-y) dx| ≤ |B_R| A B` when `F` vanishes for `|x| > R`, `|F| ≤ A`, `|G| ≤ B`
   142	(no integrability assumed: a non-integrable integrand has Bochner integral `0`). -/
   143	theorem abs_cross_le {F G : Rd d → ℝ} {R A B : ℝ} (hFR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → F x = 0)
   144	    (hA : ∀ x, |F x| ≤ A) (hB : ∀ x, |G x| ≤ B) (y : Rd d) :
   145	    |∫ x, F x * G (x - y)| ≤ A * B * volume.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) R) := by
   146	  rw [← setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (s := closedBall (0 : Rd d) R)
   147	    fun x hx => by
   148	      rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, not_le] at hx
   149	      rw [hFR x hx, zero_mul], ← Real.norm_eq_abs]
   150	  refine norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const
   151	    (measure_closedBall_lt_top (μ := (volume : Measure (Rd d))))
   152	    fun x _ => ?_
   153	  rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_mul]
   154	  exact mul_le_mul (hA x) (hB _) (abs_nonneg _) ((abs_nonneg _).trans (hA x))
   155	
   156	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (the local bound `E:positive-local-spatial-bound` of
   157	`L:positive-raw-embedding`, in bilinear form): for a locally finite `Γ` and `F`, `G` vanishing
   158	for `|x| > R` with `|F| ≤ A`, `|G| ≤ B`,
   159	`|B_Γ(F,G)| ≤ A B |B_R| Γ(B_{2R})`. -/
   160	theorem abs_spatialPair_le (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ] {F G : Rd d → ℝ}
   161	    {R A B : ℝ} (hFR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → F x = 0) (hGR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → G x = 0)
   162	    (hA : ∀ x, |F x| ≤ A) (hB : ∀ x, |G x| ≤ B) :
   163	    |spatialPair Γ F G| ≤
   164	      A * B * volume.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) R) * Γ.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) (2 * R)) := by
   165	  unfold spatialPair
   166	  rw [← setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero (s := closedBall (0 : Rd d) (2 * R))
   167	    fun y hy => by
   168	      rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, not_le] at hy
   169	      exact cross_eq_zero hFR hGR hy]
   170	  rw [← Real.norm_eq_abs]
   171	  exact norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const measure_closedBall_lt_top fun y _ => by
   172	    rw [Real.norm_eq_abs]; exact abs_cross_le hFR hA hB y

   176	theorem hasCompactSupport_of_radius {Q : Rd d → ℝ} {R : ℝ} (hQR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → Q x = 0) :
   177	    HasCompactSupport Q :=
   178	  HasCompactSupport.intro (isCompact_closedBall (0 : Rd d) R) fun x hx => by
   179	    rw [mem_closedBall, dist_zero_right, not_le] at hx
   180	    exact hQR x hx

   182	/-- Auxiliary to the Lean proof route (mollification, in place of the TeX's smooth
   183	approximation in `L:occupation-raw-square`): a continuous `Q` vanishing for `|x| > R` is

   185	theorem exists_smooth_approx {Q : Rd d → ℝ} (hQ : Continuous Q) {R : ℝ}
   186	    (hQR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → Q x = 0) {δ : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ) :
   187	    ∃ P : Rd d → ℝ, IsTestFunction P ∧ (∀ x, R + 1 < ‖x‖ → P x = 0) ∧
   188	      ∀ x, |P x - Q x| ≤ δ := by
   189	  have hQc := hasCompactSupport_of_radius hQR
   190	  obtain ⟨η, hη, hηc⟩ := Metric.uniformContinuous_iff.mp
   191	    (hQc.uniformContinuous_of_continuous hQ) δ hδ
   192	  set r : ℝ := min η 1 with hr
   193	  have hr0 : 0 < r := lt_min hη one_pos
   194	  let φ : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd d) := ⟨r / 2, r, half_pos hr0, half_lt_self hr0⟩
   195	  refine ⟨H1Density.mollify φ Q, ⟨H1Density.contDiff_mollify φ hQ.locallyIntegrable,
   196	    φ.hasCompactSupport_normed.convolution _ hQc⟩, fun x hx => ?_, fun x => ?_⟩
   197	  · by_contra hne
   198	    have hs := (support_convolution_subset (L := ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ)
   199	      (μ := volume) (f := φ.normed volume) (g := Q)) hne
   200	    rw [φ.support_normed_eq] at hs
   201	    obtain ⟨u, hu, v, hv, rfl⟩ := hs
   202	    have hu' : ‖u‖ < r := by simpa using hu
   203	    have hv' : ‖v‖ ≤ R := by
   204	      by_contra h
   205	      exact hv (hQR v (not_le.1 h))
   206	    have : ‖u + v‖ ≤ ‖u‖ + ‖v‖ := norm_add_le u v
   207	    have : r ≤ 1 := min_le_right _ _
   208	    linarith
   209	  · rw [← Real.dist_eq]
   210	    refine φ.dist_normed_convolution_le hQ.aestronglyMeasurable fun y hy => ?_
   211	    have hy' : dist y x < r := hy
   212	    exact (hηc (lt_of_lt_of_le hy' (min_le_left _ _))).le

   214	/-- **Spatial positivity for continuous compactly supported profiles** (a step of the route,
   215	auxiliary; the TeX obtains it inside the covariance space `H_sp`, `L:occupation-raw-square`):
   216	for a locally finite `Γ` with spectral measure `μ` in the manuscript's convention and a
   217	continuous `Q` vanishing for `|x| > R`, `B_Γ(Q,Q) ≥ 0`.  Route: smooth uniform approximants
   218	(mollification) with `SpatialFourLinear.spatialPair_self_nonneg`, the bilinear expansion

   220	theorem spatialPair_self_nonneg_of_continuous {Γ μ : Measure (Rd d)} [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ]
   221	    (hsp : IsSpectralMeasure Γ μ) {Q : Rd d → ℝ} (hQ : Continuous Q) {R : ℝ}
   222	    (hQR : ∀ x, R < ‖x‖ → Q x = 0) : 0 ≤ spatialPair Γ Q Q := by
   223	  have hQc := hasCompactSupport_of_radius hQR
   224	  obtain ⟨A, hA⟩ := hQ.bounded_above_of_compact_support hQc
   225	  have hA' : ∀ x, |Q x| ≤ A := fun x => by simpa using hA x
   226	  have hA0 : 0 ≤ A := (abs_nonneg _).trans (hA' 0)
   227	  set c : ℝ := volume.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) (R + 1)) *
   228	    Γ.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) (2 * (R + 1))) with hc
   229	  have hc0 : 0 ≤ c := mul_nonneg measureReal_nonneg measureReal_nonneg
   230	  have hQR1 : ∀ x, R + 1 < ‖x‖ → Q x = 0 := fun x hx => hQR x (by linarith)
   231	  refine le_of_forall_pos_le_add fun ε hε => ?_
   232	  set δ : ℝ := min 1 (ε / (c * (2 * A + 1) + 1)) with hδ
   233	  have hD : 0 < c * (2 * A + 1) + 1 := by positivity
   234	  have hδ0 : 0 < δ := lt_min one_pos (div_pos hε hD)
   235	  obtain ⟨P, hP, hPR, hPQ⟩ := exists_smooth_approx hQ hQR hδ0
   236	  set D : Rd d → ℝ := fun x => P x - Q x with hDdef
   237	  have hDc : Continuous D := hP.1.continuous.sub hQ
   238	  have hDR : ∀ x, R + 1 < ‖x‖ → D x = 0 := fun x hx => by
   239	    simp [hDdef, hPR x hx, hQR1 x hx]
   240	  have hDs := hasCompactSupport_of_radius hDR
   241	  have hquad := SpatialFourLinear.spatialPair_quad Γ hQ hQc hDc hDs 1
   242	  have hPe : (fun x => Q x + 1 * D x) = P := by funext x; simp [hDdef]
   243	  rw [hPe, one_mul, one_pow, one_mul] at hquad
   244	  have hPP := SpatialFourLinear.spatialPair_self_nonneg hsp hP
   245	  have b1 := abs_spatialPair_le Γ hQR1 hDR hA' hPQ
   246	  have b2 := abs_spatialPair_le Γ hDR hQR1 hPQ hA'
   247	  have b3 := abs_spatialPair_le Γ hDR hDR hPQ hPQ
   248	  have e1 : A * δ * volume.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) (R + 1)) *

   251	      Γ.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) (2 * (R + 1))) = c * (A * δ) := by rw [hc]; ring
   252	  have e3 : δ * δ * volume.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) (R + 1)) *
   253	      Γ.real (closedBall (0 : Rd d) (2 * (R + 1))) = c * (δ * δ) := by rw [hc]; ring

   255	  have hδ1 : δ ≤ 1 := min_le_left _ _
   256	  have hδε : δ * (c * (2 * A + 1) + 1) ≤ ε := by

   312	   98| \begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
   313	   99|   \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   314	  100|   On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   315	  101|   $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   316	  102|   h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   317	  103|   positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   318	  104|   \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   319	  105|     \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   320	  106|     =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   321	  107|     \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   322	  108|   \end{equation}
   323	  109|   It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   324	  110|   positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   325	  111| \end{proposition}
   326	  112| 
   327	  113| \begin{proof}
   328	  114|   The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   329	  115|   multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   330	  116|   -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   331	  117|   densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   332	  118|   equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   333	  119|   \[
   334	  120|     H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   335	  121|   \]
   336	  122|   The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   337	  123|   1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   338	  124|   \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   339	  125|   \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   340	  126|   $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   341	  127| 
   342	  128|   Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   343	  129|   Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   344	  130|   \[
   345	  131|     \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   346	  132|     \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   347	  133|     \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   348	  134|   \]
   349	  135|   Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   350	  136|   half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   351	  137|   equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   352	  138|   both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   353	  139|

   355	  141|   reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   356	  142|   vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite

   453	   14|   sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define

   456	   17|   \end{equation}
   457	   18|   initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
   458	   19|   representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
   459	   20|   Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
   460	   21|   positions $x$ and $x-y$.
   461	   22| \end{lemma}

   463	   24| \begin{proof}

   465	   26|   Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
   466	   27|   applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
   467	   28|   because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
   468	   29|   has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
   469	   30|   $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
   470	   31|   exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
   471	   32|   absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.

  1131	  213|     \label{E:occupation-score-ceiling}\\

  1145	  227|   supremum is zero. If $v > 0$, the derivative $\beta\sqrt{vC}T^{\beta-1}-1$

  1147	  229|   (\beta\sqrt{vC})^{1/(1-\beta)}$. The global maximum equals

/-- The time bump, supported in `(1/4, 3/4) ⊂ (0,1)`. -/
def chiB : ContDiffBump (1 / 2 : ℝ) := ⟨1 / 8, 1 / 4, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/-- The space bump on `ℝ¹`, supported in the ball of radius `2`. -/
def qB : ContDiffBump (0 : Rd 1) := ⟨1, 2, by norm_num, by norm_num⟩

/-- The separable test field `Φ(s,x) = χ(s) q(x)`. -/
def phiEx : ℝ × Rd 1 → ℝ := fun p => chiB p.1 * qB p.2

theorem phiEx_continuous : Continuous phiEx :=
  (chiB.continuous.comp continuous_fst).mul (qB.continuous.comp continuous_snd)

theorem phiEx_hasCompactSupport : HasCompactSupport phiEx := by
  refine HasCompactSupport.intro (chiB.hasCompactSupport.isCompact.prod
    qB.hasCompactSupport.isCompact) fun p hp => ?_
  simp only [phiEx]
  by_cases h1 : p.1 ∈ tsupport chiB
  · have h2 : p.2 ∉ tsupport qB := fun h2 => hp ⟨h1, h2⟩
    rw [image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport h2, mul_zero]
  · rw [image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport h1, zero_mul]

/-- Lebesgue measure on `ℝ¹` has spectral measure `δ_0` in the manuscript's convention. -/
theorem leb_spectral : IsSpectralMeasure (volume : Measure (Rd 1)) (Measure.dirac 0) := by
  intro φ
  rw [integral_dirac]
  simp

theorem leb_even : IsEven (volume : Measure (Rd 1)) := Measure.map_neg_eq_self _

theorem qB_zero {x : Rd 1} (hx : 2 < ‖x‖) : qB x = 0 :=
  qB.zero_of_le_dist (by rw [dist_zero_right]; exact hx.le)

/-- `B_Γ(q,q) = (∫ q)²` for `Γ` = Lebesgue measure. -/
theorem pair_qB : spatialPair (volume : Measure (Rd 1)) qB qB = (∫ x, qB x) * ∫ x, qB x := by
  rw [spatialPair_eq_conv volume qB.continuous qB.continuous (A := 1) (B := 1) (R := 2)
    (fun x => by rw [abs_of_nonneg qB.nonneg]; exact qB.le_one)
    (fun x => by rw [abs_of_nonneg qB.nonneg]; exact qB.le_one)
    (fun x hx => qB_zero hx) (fun x hx => qB_zero hx)]
  simp only [VariationalDilation.conv]

    18	\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Neither the test nor its covariance is changed by a
    19	physical mask. We write $h_s$ when $\Psi$ is fixed.
    98	\begin{proposition}[The unmasked Rayleigh rate]
    99	  \label{P:variational-unmasked-rate}
   100	  On complex $L^2(\R^d)$, the operator $H_s = -\Delta-h_s$ is self-adjoint on
   101	  $H^2$, with form domain $H^1$ and form $q_s(f) = \|\nabla f\|_2^2-\int
   102	  h_s|f|^2$. Its spectral bottom $E_s$ is uniformly negative on $I$. The
   103	  positive rate $\lambda_{\Psi,s} = \sqrt{-E_s}$ satisfies
   104	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-real-rayleigh}
   105	    \lambda_{\Psi,s}^2
   106	    =\sup_{\substack{f\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|f\|_2=1}}
   107	    \left(\int h_sf^2-\|\nabla f\|_2^2\right).
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	  It is Lipschitz on $I$, and $I_\Psi: = \int_0^1\lambda_{\Psi,s}\ud s$ is
   110	  positive and finite. No eigenstate at the unmasked bottom is asserted.
   111	\end{proposition}
   112	
   113	\begin{proof}
   114	  The Fourier Laplacian $A = -\Delta$ is self-adjoint on $H^2$, being
   115	  multiplication by $|\xi|^2$ with its maximal domain. Multiplication $B_s =
   116	  -h_s$ is bounded self-adjoint with norm at most $M$. Thus, $H_s = A+B_s$ is
   117	  densely defined, symmetric and closed on $H^2$; the two graph norms are
   118	  equivalent under a bounded perturbation. For real $b > M$,
   119	  \[
   120	    H_s-ib=(I+B_s(A-ib)^{-1})(A-ib).
   121	  \]
   122	  The first factor has a Neumann inverse because $\|B_s(A-ib)^{-1}\| \le M/b <
   123	  1$, and the same holds with $+ib$. To check self-adjointness directly, for $u
   124	  \in D(H_s^*)$ solve $(H_s-ib)v = (H_s^*-ib)u$ with $v \in D(H_s)$. Then $u-v
   125	  \in \ker(H_s^*-ib) = \operatorname{Ran}(H_s+ib)^\perp = \{0\}$. Hence,
   126	  $D(H_s^*) = D(H_s)$.
   127	
   128	  Set $c_{\mathrm{shift}} = 1+M$ and $J_s = H_s+c_{\mathrm{shift}} \ge 1$.
   129	  Integration by parts on $H^2$ gives
   130	  \[
   131	    \|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2=q_s(f)+c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_2^2,\qquad
   132	    \|f\|_{H^1}^2\le\|J_s^{1/2}f\|_2^2
   133	    \le c_{\mathrm{shift}}\|f\|_{H^1}^2.
   134	  \]
   135	  Spectral cutoffs $1_{[1,n]}(J_s)$ show that $H^2 = D(J_s)$ is a core for the
   136	  half-power norm; Fourier cutoffs give its density in $H^1$. Completion in the
   137	  equivalent norms identifies $D(J_s^{1/2})$ and $H^1$ as $L^2$ subspaces, since
   138	  both norms dominate $L^2$. This proves the stated form domain.
   139	
   140	  The spectral lower bound gives one direction of the Rayleigh identity. For the
   141	  reverse, nonzero spectral projections in $[E_s,E_s+\epsilon]$ give unit $H^2$
   142	  vectors with Rayleigh values at most $E_s+\epsilon$. The bottom is finite
   143	  because the operator is bounded below and has finite Rayleigh tests. Let
   144	  $\epsilon\downarrow0$. Real tests give the same infimum: $q_s(u+iv) =
   145	  q_s(u)+q_s(v)$, so the quotient is the norm-weighted average of the nonzero
   146	  real quotients. This proves the Rayleigh identity with $-E_s$ on the left. The
   147	  following negative upper bound justifies writing that value as
   148	  $\lambda_{\Psi,s}^2$ in~\eqref{E:variational-real-rayleigh}.
   149	
   150	  Proposition~\ref{P:compact-original-common-trial} supplies, for this original
   151	  $\Psi$, one unit compactly supported $w$ and a finite plateau mask with a
   152	  common strictly negative upper bound $\epsilon_0 > 0$. Its trial has support
   153	  in $B_{2L}$; choose its plateau radius $R_0 \ge 2L$. The unmasked form on this
   154	  same $w$ is no larger. Consequently, $-M \le E_s \le -\epsilon_0 < 0$, and
   155	  $\sqrt{\epsilon_0} \le \lambda_{\Psi,s} \le \sqrt M$. Comparing identical unit
   156	  form tests gives $|E_s-E_t| \le \|h_s-h_t\|_\infty$ and therefore
   157	  \[
   158	    |\lambda_{\Psi,s}-\lambda_{\Psi,t}|
   159	    \le \frac{C_\Psi}{2\sqrt{\epsilon_0}}|s-t|.
   160	  \]
   161	  This also proves positivity and finiteness of $I_\Psi$. No compact-potential
   162	  spectral theorem was applied to $H_s$. This proves
   163	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate}.
   164	\end{proof}
   270	\begin{proposition}[Intrinsic variational lower bounds]
   271	  \label{P:variational-positive-scores}
   272	  For $c > 0$, the set of variational values
   273	  $\{cI_\Psi-v_\Psi/2:\Psi\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{pos}}\}$ is nonempty and
   274	  bounded above. Its finite real supremum $S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is positive and
   275	  satisfies
   276	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-homogeneity}
   277	    S_c^{\mathrm{pos}}=c^{(4-\alpha)/(3-\alpha)}S_1^{\mathrm{pos}},
   278	    \qquad
   279	    Q_2\ge S_2^{\mathrm{pos}},
   280	  \end{equation}
   281	  where $Q_2$ is the original point liminf. The coefficient-one value is an
   282	  auxiliary variational value; no first-moment or source-constant identification
   283	  is asserted.
   284	\end{proposition}
   285	
   286	\begin{proof}
   287	  Write $k = 3-\alpha > 0$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $m = q/k > 1$. Fix one
   288	  $\Psi_0$ from the nonempty class and put $I_0 = I_{\Psi_0} > 0$, $v_0 =
   289	  v_{\Psi_0} > 0$. Positivity of the latter is
   290	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}. For $r_0 = (I_0/v_0)^{1/k} > 0$, which need
   291	  not be less than one, the exact real-power identity gives
   292	  \[
   293	    I_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}-v_{D_{r_0}\Psi_0}/2
   294	    =r_0I_0-r_0^qv_0/2=r_0I_0/2>0.
   295	  \]
   296	  This positive value is obtained from a smooth nonnegative control.
   297	
   298	  For $c > 0$ put $r_c = c^{1/k}$ and $K_c = c^m > 0$.
   299	  Lemma~\ref{L:variational-control-dilation} and the exact scalar powers give,
   300	  for every $\Psi$,
   301	  \begin{equation}\label{E:variational-score-set-scaling}
   302	    cI_{D_{r_c}\Psi}-v_{D_{r_c}\Psi}/2
   303	    =K_c(I_\Psi-v_\Psi/2).
   304	  \end{equation}
   305	  Since $D_{r_c}$ is a bijection of the entire class, the whole set of
   306	  variational values with coefficient $c$ is $K_c$ times the whole
   307	  coefficient-one set of variational values.
   308	
   309	  We prove boundedness before taking finite-real suprema. The independent
   310	  Theorem~\ref{T:full-upper}, for the \emph{same canonical solution}, gives
   311	  \[
   312	    \E|u(T,0)|^2\le e(T+2)^d e^{C_{\mathrm{up}}T^\kappa},
   313	    \qquad T\ge1,\quad C_{\mathrm{up}}<\infty.
   314	  \]
   315	  Its prefactor is negligible: choose $\epsilon = \kappa/2 > 0$, use $\log T \le
   316	  (T^\epsilon-1)/\epsilon$ and $\log(T+2) \le \log T+\log3$ for $T \ge 1$, and
   317	  divide by $T^\kappa$. Thus, the original point limsup is at most
   318	  $C_{\mathrm{up}}$. One fixed test/mask lower bound gives a finite lower bound
   319	  for $Q_2$, so $Q_2$ is finite. By~\eqref{E:variational-unmasked-point-lower}
   320	  every coefficient-two variational expression is at most this same $Q_2 \le
   321	  C_{\mathrm{up}}$, uniformly in $\Psi$.
   322	  Equation~\eqref{E:variational-score-set-scaling} at $c = 2$ consequently
   323	  bounds all coefficient-one variational values by $C_{\mathrm{up}}/K_2$. The
   324	  nonempty set has a finite real supremum $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} > 0$ by the
   325	  positive test above.
   326	
   327	  For general $c$, set equality and $K_c > 0$ show that $K_cS_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   328	  is the supremum: it is an upper bound, and every smaller number is exceeded by
   329	  $K_c$ times a coefficient-one variational expression within the corresponding
   330	  positive distance of its supremum. This proves finiteness, positivity and the
   331	  first identity in~\eqref{E:variational-score-homogeneity}. Taking the
   332	  numerical supremum of the coefficient-two lower bounds proves the second.
   333	  Although $2^m > 2$, the resulting $S_2^{\mathrm{pos}} > 2S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$
   334	  is only a comparison of auxiliary variational values. It is not a Jensen
   335	  improvement without a first-moment identification. This proves
   336	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
   337	\end{proof}
   398	\begin{lemma}[The original mean and variance]\label{L:compact-raw-profile}
   399	  Let $\Gamma \ne 0$ satisfy Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog}, let $a = \alpha_0$, and
   400	  let real nonnegative nonzero $\Psi \in C_c^\infty((0,1)\times\R^d)$ be
   401	  arbitrary, without a separability assumption. Define
   402	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-mean}
   403	    h_\sigma(x)=\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}
   404	    (\Gamma*\Psi(u,\cdot))(x)\ud u,\qquad
   405	    \overline{q}(x)=\int_0^1\Psi(u,x)\ud u,\qquad Z=W(\Psi).
   406	  \end{equation}
   407	  Then $h$ is smooth in time and space on compact sets, and
   408	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-raw-cost}
   409	    0<v_\Psi:=\E Z^2
   410	    =\int_0^1\int\Psi(\sigma,x)h_\sigma(x)\ud x\ud\sigma<\infty.
   411	  \end{equation}
   412	  Against every smooth compact positive-time test $F_0$,
   413	  \[
   414	    \E[W(\Psi)W(F_0)]=\int F_0(s,x)h_s(x)\ud x\ud s.
   415	  \]
   416	  Moreover, on $I$,
   417	  \begin{equation}\label{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}
   418	    h_\sigma\ge\Gamma*\overline{q},\qquad
   419	    v_\Psi\ge Q(\overline{q})
   420	    :=\int\Gamma(\ud z)\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x>0.
   421	  \end{equation}
   422	  For every fixed mask, $V_\sigma = m_Rh_\sigma$ is a smooth compact family,
   423	  Lipschitz in $\sigma$ in $L^\infty$ and $L^2$.
   424	\end{lemma}
   425	
   426	\begin{proof}
   427	  Choose $A \ge 1$ containing the spatial support of $\Psi$ in $B_A$. The
   428	  original covariance identity and absolute Fubini give the stated mean pairing:
   429	  the two compact tests restrict spatial differences to a compact set of finite
   430	  $\Gamma$ mass, and the time singularity is locally integrable since $a < 1$.
   431	  This identifies the linear covariance mean without evaluating noise at a
   432	  point. The same calculation gives~\eqref{E:compact-raw-cost}. Its spatial
   433	  integrand is bounded in integral by
   434	  $\|\Psi\|_\infty^2|B_A|\Gamma(\overline{B}_{2A})$, and
   435	  $\int_0^1\int_0^1|\sigma-u|^{-a}\ud u\ud\sigma = 2/((1-a)(2-a))$, proving
   436	  finiteness.
   437	
   438	  Nonnegative nonzero smooth $\Psi$ has positive integral, so $\overline{q} \ne
   439	  0$. Nonzero $\Gamma$ charges some ball, and homogeneity gives $\Gamma(B_1) =
   440	  r^{\alpha-d}\Gamma(B_r) > 0$. Thus, every origin-centered ball $B_r$, $r > 0$,
   441	  has positive finite mass. The continuous compact autocorrelation
   442	  $\int\overline{q}(x)\overline{q}(x-z)\ud x$ is positive at zero and bounded
   443	  below on some ball. This proves $0 < Q(\overline{q}) < \infty$. Since
   444	  $|\sigma-u|^{-a} \ge 1$ on the unit time square, positive Tonelli gives both
   445	  inequalities in~\eqref{E:compact-positive-mean-floor}.
   446	
   447	  Extend $\Psi$ by zero in time and write
   448	  \[
   449	    h_s(x)=\int_\R |r|^{-a}
   450	    \int\Gamma(\ud z)\Psi(s-r,x-z)\ud r.
   451	  \]
   452	  On compact $s,x$ sets the relevant $r,z$ range over fixed compact sets;
   453	  $|r|^{-a}$ is integrable there. Every derivative falls on the smooth test, not
   454	  on the singular time kernel. Dominated differentiation gives smoothness and
   455	  continuity of all derivatives on compacts. Multiplication by $m_R$ now gives
   456	  the claimed compact family and its fixed-$R$ Lipschitz bounds. This proves
   457	  Lemma~\ref{L:compact-raw-profile}.
   458	\end{proof}

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}

    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on

    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in

    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}

    42	  \[

    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).

    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =

    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a

    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of

   101	\begin{lemma}[Deterministic Fourier bound for the spatial energy]
   102	  \label{L:spatial-fourier-bound}

   104	  $g\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R)$ satisfy $\|g\|_2=1$ and put
   105	  $b=\|\nabla g\|_2^2$. Then $b>0$ and
   106	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-fourier-bound}
   107	    0\le A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)
   108	    \le 2^{1+\alpha}R_\alpha b^{\alpha/2},
   109	  \end{equation}
   110	  where $R_\alpha$ is defined in~\eqref{E:intro-spectral-mass}.

   113	\begin{proof}

   115	  and compact support forces $g=0$, contrary to $\|g\|_2=1$. Put $Q=g^2$ and
   116	  use the unnormalized Fourier transform
   117	  \[
   118	    \mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)=\int_{\R^d}e^{-i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x.
   119	  \]
   120	  In the unitary convention of Section~\ref{S:masked-covariance}, this is
   121	  $c_d^{-1}\widehat Q$, with $c_d=(2\pi)^{-d/2}$.
   122	  The autocorrelation
   123	  \[
   124	    c_Q(y)=\int_{\R^d}Q(x)Q(x-y)\ud x
   125	  \]
   126	  is smooth and compactly supported. Apply the distributional spectral
   127	  identity~\eqref{E:masked-spectral-convention} to this Schwartz function.
   128	  Its inner Fourier integral is $|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2$, since $Q$ is real.
   129	  Hence
   130	  \[
   131	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)=\int c_Q(y)\Gamma(\ud y)
   132	    =\int|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi).
   133	  \]

   135	  Radon, while $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|^2$ is Schwartz and $\mu$ is tempered.
   136	  No density of either measure is required.
   137	
   138	  Since $\|Q\|_1=1$, we have $|\mathcal{F}_0Q|\le1$. Integration by parts
   139	  and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality give
   140	  \[
   141	    |\xi|\,|\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|
   142	    \le\|\nabla Q\|_1
   143	    \le2\|g\|_2\|\nabla g\|_2=2\sqrt b.
   144	  \]

   146	  \[
   147	    |\mathcal{F}_0Q(\xi)|^2\le\frac{8b}{4b+|\xi|^2}.

   150	  Lemma~\ref{L:damped-homogeneous-norms}, together

   164	\end{proof}

   166	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
   167	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}

   169	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is

   179	\begin{proof}

   181	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   182	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   183	  autocorrelation argument in the proof of
   184	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} gives

   188	  finiteness of $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$. It remains to prove the score inequality.
   189	  With $U_\ell g(x)=\ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the physical changes of variables give
   190	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   191	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   192	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   193	  \end{equation}
   194	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   195	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   196	
   197	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   198	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   199	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   200	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   201	  \[
   202	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   203	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   204	  \]
   205	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   206	  gives
   207	  \[
   208	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   209	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   210	  \]
   211	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   212	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   213	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. This argument retains the finite
   214	  real value $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ fixed at the start of the section; only the
   215	  proof of $R_0<\infty$ is independent of that input. This proves
   216	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   217	\end{proof}

   219	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   220	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   221	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   222	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   223	  \begin{align}
   224	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   225	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   226	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   227	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   228	  \end{align}
   229	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   230	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   231	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   232	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   233	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   234	  \end{equation}
   235	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   236	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   237	\end{proposition}
   238	
   239	\begin{proof}
   240	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   241	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   242	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   243	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   244	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   245	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   246	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   247	  convention gives
   248	  \[
   249	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   250	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   251	  \]
   252	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   253	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   254	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   255	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   256	  \[
   257	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   258	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   259	  \]
   260	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   261	
   262	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   263	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   264	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   265	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   266	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   267	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   268	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   269	
   270	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   271	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   272	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   273	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   274	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   275	  continuity.
   276	
   277	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   278	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   279	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   280	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   281	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   282	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   283	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   284	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   285	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   286	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   287	
   288	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   289	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   290	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   291	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   292	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   293	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   294	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   295	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   296	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   297	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   298	\end{proof}
   299	
   300	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   301	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   302	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   303	  \[
   304	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   305	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   306	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   307	  \]
   308	  Then
   309	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   310	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   311	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   312	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   313	    \in(0,\infty).
   314	  \end{equation}
   315	  In particular,
   316	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   317	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   318	    \qquad
   319	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   320	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   321	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   322	  \end{equation}
   323	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   324	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   325	\end{proposition}
   326	
   327	\begin{proof}
   328	  Physical change of variables, or smooth approximation and
   329	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, extends \eqref{E:spatial-dilation} to
   330	  real $H^1$ profiles. For fixed unit $g$, with $A,b > 0$, the maximum of
   331	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals
   332	  \[
   333	    \frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   334	    R(g)^{2/(2-\alpha)}.
   335	  \]
   336	  Dilation preserves the whole unit class and includes $\ell = 1$. Taking both
   337	  numerical suprema, then profiles with ratio tending to $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$,
   338	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. No optimizer is assumed. Smooth ratios
   339	  also approach $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   340	  Pass them through~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score} and substitute
   341	  \[
   342	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}\alpha^{\alpha/2}
   343	    =\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2-\alpha}
   344	    \right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}.
   345	  \]
   346	  This gives~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. This proves
   347	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-energy-map}.
   348	\end{proof}
   225	\begin{hypothesis}[Homogeneous covariance]\label{H:homog}
   226	  Let $d \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $0 < \alpha_0 < 1$. The spatial covariance is a
   227	  nonnegative, even, positive-definite tempered Radon measure $\Gamma$ on
   228	  $\R^d$, with positive even tempered Radon spectral measure $\mu$ in the
   229	  convention
   230	  \[
   231	    \Gamma=\int e^{i\xi\cdot x}\mu(\ud\xi)
   232	    \quad\text{in the sense of tempered distributions}.
   233	  \]
   234	  The symbol $\gamma$ in~\eqref{E:cov} denotes this covariance as a function
   235	  when one exists, and as a distribution otherwise. For every Borel set $A$ and
   236	  $c > 0$, $\Gamma(cA) = c^{d-\alpha}\Gamma(A)$, and
   237	  \begin{equation}\label{E:threshold}
   238	    \alpha_0+\alpha<2,
   239	  \end{equation}
   240	  with $0 < \alpha < d$, or $\alpha = d = 1$. In particular, the last case
   241	  includes spatial white noise $\Gamma = \delta_0$.
   242	\end{hypothesis}

   105	def coef (alpha b : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   106	  (4 - alpha - 2 * b) ^ ((4 - alpha - 2 * b) / 2) / (8 * (4 - alpha - b) ^ (4 - alpha - b))
   107

   111	def Fb (alpha b z : ℝ) : ℝ :=
   112	  (3 - alpha) * (coef alpha b * (2 * z / (2 - alpha)) ^ ((2 - alpha) / 2)) ^ (1 / (3 - alpha))
